newsitem.title: USA: Niagara Mohawk debt holder hopeful on IPPs.
newsitem.headline: Niagara Mohawk debt holder hopeful on IPPs.

text.p: One Niagara Mohawk Power Corp debt holder remains hopeful the utility will reach an agreement with independent power producers this month.

"The only thing that stands in the way is too many chefs ruining the stew," according to Barry E. Welch, a senior investment officer at John Hancock Mutual Life Insurance Co. He is head of the energy section in the company's Bond and Corporate Finance Department.
Welch is involved in Niagara Mohawk's talks with the independent power producers since Hancock holds the utility's mortgage bonds and debt of some of the IPPs.

On January 30, the utility delayed reporting 1996 fourth quarter and year results and declaring its first quarter preferred stock dividends citing the unresolved nature of the IPP talks and related accounting issues.
Thursday Niagara Mohawk spokeswoman Kerry Burns said there has been no decision on whether the company will seek to delay reporting 1996 results beyond this month.
Under U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission rules, the company has 90 days -- until the end of March -- to report results or request an extension.
Asked what the utility planned to do, Burns said "that hasn't been decided yet."

In testimony Wednesday to the New York state Senate Energy Committee, the IPPs' representative said "these negotiations are far from over and part of the difficulty in coming up with a viable deal is the ability of a utility to raise capital and for IPPs to refinance their loans ... and serious doubts existing in the investment community about stranded cost recovery in New York State."

Carol Murphy, executive director of the Independent Power Producers of New York told the hearing: "Components being discussed (in the negotiations with Niagara Mohawk) include renegotiated power purchase agreements which reduce a utility's overall financial commitment to outright buyouts of existing operating power plants to major restructurings of (natural gas purchase) agreements."
